answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a minimum bond before it may accept paid work. A contract releases the bond when the agent delivers a verifiable result, but slashes it if an agreed, checkable condition is breached. If ember, delta, and juniper are three identities controlled by one attacker, each still needs its own bond; creating more identities therefore ties up more capital, and cheating risks losing it. This raises the cost of a Sybil attack without pretending to prove who owns each identity.
